text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Jawad al-Anani announces borders of planned free trade zone in Aqaba.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali confirms the importance of continuing Palestinian-Israeli negotiations.
- Work started on establishing eight factories in Jordan's poorer southern region which will offer work to 550 people.
- Egyptian embassy urges all Egyptian workers in Jordan to get work permits by May 31 deadline.
- Journalists union committee resigns in protest at new press law. Head of lawyers' union says law is unconstitutional.
- Water Ministry official says irrigated land in Jordan Valley may be distributed within two months.
- Lawyer for Jordanian soldier who shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls invites Arab lawyers to join in defence of "The Baqoura Soldier".
- All Jordanians in Zaire are safe, Kinshasa hotel manager says.
- Finance Minister Suleiman al-Hafez says ministry should have plan by September for merging pensions law with social security law.
- Journalists, opposition parties in uproar over new press and publications law. Editors of weekly papers plan to file case at higher court of justice.
